stem: (Select TWO.) A platform engineer at Solace Freight runs `terraform init -upgrade` on a configuration with a committed dependency lock file, then notices a teammate's plain `terraform init` on the same commit produced a different provider version. Which two facts explain this?

choices.text: `-upgrade` disregards the versions recorded in the dependency lock file
The dependency lock file constrains only how a later deployment step behaves, and has no effect on installing providers during init
`-upgrade` installs the newest available provider version that still satisfies the configured version constraints
A plain re-run without `-upgrade` also disregards the dependency lock file every time
The dependency lock file is regenerated with a randomly chosen provider version on every re-run

rationale: `-upgrade` disregards the lock file's recorded selections and installs the newest version that still satisfies the constraints, which is why the two teammates ended up with different versions. The lock file governs `init`'s own provider installation directly, not some later step. A plain re-run without `-upgrade` respects the lock file rather than disregarding it, which is the entire point of committing one. The lock file records a specific selection; it is not randomized on each run.
